title: Synthetic Reproduction and Augmentation of COVID-19 Case Reporting Data by Agent-Based Simulation

key_points.claim: Population aspect: the model maps Austria's ~9M inhabitants as agents with demographically representative properties; demographic events (death, childbirth) are stochastic and event-driven.
key_points.evidence_quote: we map the population of Austria (approximately nine million inhabitants) with agents that correctly represent the demographic properties of the country

key_points.claim: Social structure/interaction: daily face-to-face contacts occur in virtual groups (households, workplaces, schools, leisure), aligned to demographic, commuting, density and class-size data.
key_points.evidence_quote: face-to-face encounters which occur on a daily basis in virtual groups that represent workplaces, schools, households and leisure-time

key_points.claim: Institutions/policy: a manually recorded timeline of government countermeasures modulates agent behavior; awareness effects need heuristic modeling.
key_points.evidence_quote: we use a manually recorded timeline of the implementation and expiration of administrative policies to modulate the behavior of agents

key_points.claim: Calibration/validation: calibrated to the first wave cumulative confirmed cases; validated against independent hospitalization, fatality, age and mobility data. Calibrated infection probability of 5% per contact is close to the literature value of 4.4%.
key_points.evidence_quote: the infection probability during face-to-face contact has been calibrated to 5%, resembling a value of 4.4%

key_points.claim: Individual behavior/pathways: agents follow branching disease/treatment pathways (symptoms, testing, hospitalization, isolation) with transition times set from medical data.
key_points.evidence_quote: agents go through a pathway that depicts different stages of the disease and treatment

key_points.claim: Use as data augmentation: the simulation yields 98,342 virtual patients versus 20,797 reported cases, revealing unreported cases and age-related under-reporting in younger groups.
key_points.evidence_quote: the number of records (including unreported cases) in the synthetic data set (98,342)

key_points.claim: Limitations: fatalities are decided retrospectively, which produces a time delay in the death curve. The data are a statistical sample and cannot reconstruct the model inputs.
key_points.evidence_quote: the curve displays a significant time delay

key_points.claim: Future work: scenario testing of vaccination and lockdown policies, plus transmission clusters with geographic and socio-structural information.
key_points.evidence_quote: We intend to provide synthetic data on transmission clusters in combination with geographic and socio-structural information

reliability_notes: Full text was available. It is a preprint, so it is not peer reviewed. It is an epidemiological ABM with a synthetic population, and it is only tangentially about artificial societies in general. Validation is limited, and much of the validation data is not public.
